coach.headline: You’re often entering junctions on red
coach.pattern: It tends to happen when you’re either in the bike lane or the traffic lane and you reach the stop line before the signal turns green. You usually move forward while the light is still red, sometimes even when a vehicle is close by or a bus is travelling straight through.
coach.why_it_matters: Going into the junction on red puts you into the path of traffic that has the right of way, raising the chance of a close‑call or collision.
drills: Pause at every stop line and look for the green light before you move.
Use the road markings as a visual cue to stay back until the signal changes.
Practice checking all directions for traffic, even when you’re in a bike lane, before you cross.

coach.headline: You often ride on the sidewalk
coach.pattern: Most of the times you end up on the sidewalk when there is no visible traffic signal and you are close to pedestrians. It tends to happen in low‑light conditions and when a bus or car is about to enter the area you are using.
coach.why_it_matters: Being on the sidewalk puts you near walkers and can make drivers less likely to see you, raising the chance of a collision.
drills: Before you start a stretch, check that the road or cycle lane is clear and choose that instead of the pavement.
When you must use the pavement, stay close to the edge, keep a safe gap from pedestrians and scan ahead for any vehicles about to turn or enter.
In dim conditions, switch on a bright front light and wear reflective gear, then pause at any junction to confirm the road is safe before moving back.

coach.headline: Watch your line changes
coach.pattern: You were in the traffic lane and shifted sideways just as a large vehicle was overtaking you on the right, closing to about half a metre. The move placed you directly in the truck’s path, leaving very little clearance.
coach.why_it_matters: Changing line into traffic can dramatically cut the safe distance between you and a fast‑moving vehicle, raising the risk of a serious collision.
drills: Stay in your lane until you clearly see a safe gap ahead.
Scan behind and to the side before moving sideways.
Signal early and only shift when the gap is comfortably wide.

overview.summary: You’re making good progress, but there are a few habits that could be safer. Most of your rides show you’re often entering junctions on red and riding on the pavement, which can put you at risk. A few small adjustments will help you feel more confident and stay safer on the road.
priorities: Wait for the signal facing you to turn green before crossing any junction
Stay on the road rather than the sidewalk whenever possible
Check the gap carefully before changing your line into traffic
overview.encouragement: Keep up the effort – each improvement makes a big difference.
